--- title: "Quarterback yardage keeps climbing across a college career while running back yardage peaks and receiver yardage slows" date: "2026-11-05" description: "Median passing yardage rises through every career season in the data while rushing yardage peaks in the fourth season and receiving yardage grows only slowly after it, and running back yardage falls the most against stronger opponents." followups: - "Position-specific baselines: adjust each group against its own position rather than every player with a line in the category." - "Split the career arcs by whether a player was eventually drafted, to see when the drafted and undrafted paths separate." - "Carry a second stat per group (quarterback rushing, running back receiving) so a group is not reduced to one dimension." author: - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco" freeze: auto vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Quarterback yardage keeps climbing across a college career while running back yardage peaks and receiver yardage slows} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # ---- Packages, data connection and figure defaults ------------------------- # Load the project's functions straight from the checkout with pkgload; the # repo is never installed (decision 0042). The site build sets CFB2NFL_ROOT, # a local render finds the checkout from the working directory. root <- Sys.getenv("CFB2NFL_ROOT") if (!nzchar(root)) root <- pkgload::pkg_path() knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root) pkgload::load_all(root, quiet = TRUE) con <- DBI::dbConnect( duckdb::duckdb(), file.path(root, "data", "cfb2nfl.duckdb"), read_only = TRUE ) library(DBI) library(dplyr) library(duckdb) library(ggiraph) library(ggplot2) library(knitr) # One interaction style for every girafe figure: a clear hover pop, dimming # of non-hovered marks, a dark tooltip, and toolbar zoom + PNG download. set_girafe_defaults( opts_hover = opts_hover( css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);" ), opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"), opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip( css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;" ), opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5), opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"), opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE) ) # thousands-separated and percent formatters for inline numbers fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) { formatC(as.numeric(x), big.mark = ",", format = "f", digits = digits) } pct <- function(x, digits = 1) sprintf("%.*f%%", digits, 100 * x) # ---- Load the tables ------------------------------------------------------- # Season arcs and game production are built here from the tested package # functions (decision 0037). The season index counts every season with any # stat line, so the arcs need the full long stats, not just the yardage rows. # Roster carries the position label used to form the three groups. pg <- dbReadTable(con, "player_game") sa <- dbGetQuery( con, "SELECT playerId, player, season, team, category, statType, stat FROM player_stats" ) |> build_season_arcs() gp <- build_game_production(pg) rost <- dbReadTable(con, "roster") band_levels <- c( "Under 1400", "1400 to 1599", "1600 to 1799", "1800 and up", "Unrated" ) group_levels <- c("Quarterbacks", "Running backs", "Receivers") # Each position group is tracked by one signature yardage stat: a quarterback # by passing, a running back by rushing, a receiver by receiving. The group # palette is reused in every figure so group always means the same colour. sig <- tibble::tribble( ~pos , ~group , ~game_stat , ~category , ~label , "QB" , "Quarterbacks" , "pass_yds" , "passing" , "Passing yards" , "RB" , "Running backs" , "rush_yds" , "rushing" , "Rushing yards" , "WR" , "Receivers" , "rec_yds" , "receiving" , "Receiving yards" ) group_pal <- c( Quarterbacks = "#4C78A8", `Running backs` = "#E45756", Receivers = "#54A24B" ) # One group per player: the position he appears at most often on a roster, # restricted to the three offensive skill positions (key on athlete id). pos <- rost |> filter(.data$position %in% c("QB", "RB", "WR")) |> count(.data$playerId, .data$position) |> group_by(.data$playerId) |> slice_max(.data$n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup() |> transmute(.data$playerId, pos = .data$position) # Signature season arcs: season totals in each group's signature category. cast_sa <- sa |> filter(.data$statType == "YDS") |> inner_join(pos, by = "playerId") |> inner_join( sig |> select("pos", "category", "group", "label"), by = c("pos", "category") ) |> mutate(group = factor(.data$group, group_levels)) # Signature game production, carrying the opponent-adjusted residual. cast_gp <- gp |> inner_join(pos, by = "playerId") |> inner_join( sig |> select("pos", game_stat = "game_stat", "group"), by = c("pos", stat = "game_stat") ) |> mutate( group = factor(.data$group, group_levels), band = factor(.data$opponent_elo_band, band_levels) ) # ---- Numbers quoted in the prose ------------------------------------------- # Every figure and inline number is computed here from the database. # Opponent Elo distribution and the band each cutoff carves out. The cutoffs # are even 200-point Elo steps (1400 / 1600 / 1800); this shows how many games # and what Elo range land in each so the choice can be read off the data. elo_median <- median(pg$opponent_pregame_elo, na.rm = TRUE) elo_bands <- pg |> mutate( band = factor(opponent_elo_band(.data$opponent_pregame_elo), band_levels) ) |> group_by(.data$band) |> summarise( games = dplyr::n(), min_elo = min(.data$opponent_pregame_elo), max_elo = max(.data$opponent_pregame_elo), .groups = "drop" ) |> arrange(.data$band) # Population of each group: distinct players, season lines, and game lines. grp_pop <- sig |> mutate(group = factor(.data$group, group_levels)) |> select("group", "label") |> left_join( cast_sa |> group_by(.data$group) |> summarise( players = dplyr::n_distinct(.data$playerId), season_lines = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ), by = "group" ) |> left_join( cast_gp |> count(.data$group, name = "game_lines"), by = "group" ) |> arrange(.data$group) # Viz 1: career arcs. Median signature yards by career season, keeping only the # season indices where every group still has at least 50 players. arc_n <- cast_sa |> count(.data$group, .data$season_index) keep_idx <- arc_n |> group_by(.data$season_index) |> summarise(m = min(.data$n), .groups = "drop") |> filter(.data$m >= 50) |> pull(.data$season_index) arc_med <- cast_sa |> filter(.data$season_index %in% keep_idx) |> group_by(.data$group, .data$season_index) |> summarise( med = median(.data$value), q1 = quantile(.data$value, 0.25), q3 = quantile(.data$value, 0.75), players = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ) max_idx <- max(keep_idx) qb_arc <- arc_med |> filter(.data$group == "Quarterbacks") qb_med_1 <- qb_arc$med[qb_arc$season_index == 1] qb_med_max <- qb_arc$med[qb_arc$season_index == max_idx] rb_arc <- arc_med |> filter(.data$group == "Running backs") rb_med_peak <- max(rb_arc$med) rb_peak_idx <- rb_arc$season_index[which.max(rb_arc$med)] wr_arc <- arc_med |> filter(.data$group == "Receivers") wr_med_at_rb_peak <- wr_arc$med[wr_arc$season_index == rb_peak_idx] wr_med_max <- wr_arc$med[wr_arc$season_index == max_idx] # Viz 2: opponent-band gradient. Mean signature yards per game by group x band, # with a +/- 1 SD range marking how much games vary within each band. band_grad <- cast_gp |> group_by(.data$group, .data$band) |> summarise( mean_yds = mean(.data$value), sd_yds = sd(.data$value), games = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate( lo = pmax(.data$mean_yds - .data$sd_yds, 0), hi = .data$mean_yds + .data$sd_yds ) rated <- band_grad |> filter(.data$band != "Unrated") drop_tbl <- rated |> group_by(.data$group) |> summarise( drop = mean_yds[.data$band == "Under 1400"] - mean_yds[.data$band == "1800 and up"], .groups = "drop" ) qb_drop <- drop_tbl$drop[drop_tbl$group == "Quarterbacks"] rb_drop <- drop_tbl$drop[drop_tbl$group == "Running backs"] wr_drop <- drop_tbl$drop[drop_tbl$group == "Receivers"] # Quarterback means across the three lower rated bands, before the top band. qb_rated <- rated |> filter(.data$group == "Quarterbacks") qb_low_range <- range(qb_rated$mean_yds[qb_rated$band != "1800 and up"]) qb_top <- qb_rated$mean_yds[qb_rated$band == "1800 and up"] # Viz 3: residual spread. The residual is opponent- and season-adjusted, so it # centres near zero by construction; the spread is what differs by group. resid_spread <- cast_gp |> group_by(.data$group) |> summarise( games = dplyr::n(), sd = sd(.data$residual), iqr = IQR(.data$residual), p90 = quantile(.data$residual, 0.9), # Spread relative to the group's own typical game, so groups on different # yardage scales compare. rel_sd = sd(.data$residual) / mean(.data$value), .groups = "drop" ) qb_sd <- resid_spread$sd[resid_spread$group == "Quarterbacks"] wr_sd <- resid_spread$sd[resid_spread$group == "Receivers"] rel <- function(g) resid_spread$rel_sd[resid_spread$group == g] rel_most <- resid_spread$group[which.max(resid_spread$rel_sd)] # Per-group x band residual summary, for the exploratory boxplot tooltips. resid_box <- cast_gp |> group_by(.data$group, .data$band) |> summarise( med = median(.data$residual), q1 = quantile(.data$residual, 0.25), q3 = quantile(.data$residual, 0.75), games = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop" ) |> mutate( tip = paste0( .data$group, ", ", .data$band, ": median ", fmt(.data$med), ", IQR ", fmt(.data$q1), " to ", fmt(.data$q3), " over ", fmt(.data$games), " games" ) ) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} *Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-11-07. Careers of recent classes are right-censored; later seasons may not yet be present.* ::: ## 1. Introduction A player's yardage moves from season to season and game to game, and both the stage of his career and the strength of his opponent are reasons. This post follows three offensive groups, quarterbacks, running backs and receivers, and asks three descriptive questions of the data: how does each group's production grow across a college career, how does it change as opponents get stronger, and how much does it swing from game to game once opponent strength is held constant. ## 2. Data ### 2.1 Each game is set against the league baseline for its opponent strength Each player-game is compared with the average for the same season, stat and opponent band. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Term , ~Meaning , "Position group" , "Quarterbacks, running backs, or receivers, from the player's most frequent roster position." , "Signature stat" , "The yardage that defines a group: passing (QB), rushing (RB), receiving (WR)." , "Season arc" , "Season total of the signature stat, one per season." , "Season index" , "The player's n-th season with a stat line in the data (career season)." , "Opponent band" , "The opponent's pregame Elo: under 1400, 1400 to 1599, 1600 to 1799, 1800 and up, or unrated (no Elo)." , "Baseline" , "Mean yards for that season, band, and stat across all players with a line in the category." , "Residual" , "A game's yards minus its baseline." ) |> kable(caption = "The terms used in the post.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: The terms used in the post. |Term |Meaning | |:--------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |Position group |Quarterbacks, running backs, or receivers, from the player's most frequent roster position. | |Signature stat |The yardage that defines a group: passing (QB), rushing (RB), receiving (WR). | |Season arc |Season total of the signature stat, one per season. | |Season index |The player's n-th season with a stat line in the data (career season). | |Opponent band |The opponent's pregame Elo: under 1400, 1400 to 1599, 1600 to 1799, 1800 and up, or unrated (no Elo). | |Baseline |Mean yards for that season, band, and stat across all players with a line in the category. | |Residual |A game's yards minus its baseline. | ::: ::: ### 2.2 Opponent Elo is split into even 200-point bands Elo is CFBD's pregame team-strength rating: a higher number is a stronger opponent, and the rating is recentred each week so the median rated team sits near 1,508. The bands are even 200-point steps at 1400, 1600 and 1800, chosen so each covers the same width of the scale rather than the same number of games. The table and histogram below show the resulting split: opponents CFBD does not rate (mostly FCS and lower-division teams) have no Elo and form their own unrated band rather than being dropped. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} elo_bands |> transmute( `Opponent band` = .data$band, `Player-games` = fmt(.data$games), `Lowest Elo` = ifelse(is.finite(.data$min_elo), fmt(.data$min_elo), "--"), `Highest Elo` = ifelse(is.finite(.data$max_elo), fmt(.data$max_elo), "--") ) |> kable( caption = "Player-game stat lines (all players and stats) and the Elo range in each opponent band." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Player-game stat lines (all players and stats) and the Elo range in each opponent band. |Opponent band |Player-games |Lowest Elo |Highest Elo | |:-------------|:------------|:----------|:-----------| |Under 1400 |225,673 |528 |1,399 | |1400 to 1599 |216,937 |1,400 |1,599 | |1600 to 1799 |160,562 |1,600 |1,799 | |1800 and up |77,636 |1,800 |2,415 | |Unrated |208,134 |-- |-- | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pg |> filter(!is.na(.data$opponent_pregame_elo)) |> ggplot(aes(.data$opponent_pregame_elo)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 25, fill = "#4C78A8") + geom_vline( xintercept = c(1400, 1600, 1800), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8 ) + annotate( "text", x = c(1300, 1500, 1700, 2000), y = Inf, vjust = 1.6, label = c("Under 1400", "1400 to 1599", "1600 to 1799", "1800 and up"), size = 4 ) + labs(x = "Opponent pregame Elo", y = "Player-games") + theme_cfb2nfl() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](2026-11-05-performance-arcs_files/figure-html/s22-hist-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ### 2.3 Each group is tracked by one signature stat A quarterback is read by his passing yards, a running back by his rushing yards, and a receiver by his receiving yards. All three groups are large enough to summarise. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} grp_pop |> transmute( `Position group` = .data$group, `Signature stat` = .data$label, Players = fmt(.data$players), `Season lines` = fmt(.data$season_lines), `Game lines` = fmt(.data$game_lines) ) |> kable(caption = "The three groups and the size of each population.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: The three groups and the size of each population. |Position group |Signature stat |Players |Season lines |Game lines | |:--------------|:---------------|:-------|:------------|:----------| |Quarterbacks |Passing yards |3,602 |8,869 |47,962 | |Running backs |Rushing yards |6,542 |16,085 |97,117 | |Receivers |Receiving yards |10,845 |25,562 |143,931 | ::: ::: ## 3. Results ### 3.1 Quarterback yardage keeps climbing across a career while running backs peak and receivers slow Median passing yards rise at every career season shown, from 119 in a quarterback's first season to 1,706 by his 6th, while the rushing median peaks at 282 yards in season 4 and the receiving median edges from 282 to 304 after it. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} arc_med |> transmute( `Position group` = .data$group, `Season index` = .data$season_index, `Median yards` = fmt(.data$med), `Middle 50%` = paste0(fmt(.data$q1), " to ", fmt(.data$q3)), Players = fmt(.data$players) ) |> ``` ::: ::: ### 3.2 Running back yardage falls the most against stronger opponents, while quarterbacks dip only against the strongest From the weakest rated band to the strongest, mean yards per game fall about 10 for running backs, 2 for receivers and 8 for quarterbacks, whose mean holds between 165.8 and 167.9 until the top band (158.2). The point and range on each bar mark the mean and plus or minus one standard deviation of game-to-game yards, so the spread can be read beside the average. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} band_grad |> transmute( `Position group` = .data$group, `Opponent band` = .data$band, `Mean yards per game` = fmt(.data$mean_yds, 1), Games = fmt(.data$games) ) |> arrange(`Position group`, `Opponent band`) |> kable( caption = "Mean signature yards per game by group and opponent band. Unrated opponents (no Elo) are not the weakest rated band and are left out of the drop comparison." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Mean signature yards per game by group and opponent band. Unrated opponents (no Elo) are not the weakest rated band and are left out of the drop comparison. |Position group |Opponent band |Mean yards per game |Games | |:--------------|:-------------|:-------------------|:------| |Quarterbacks |Under 1400 |165.8 |11,396 | |Quarterbacks |1400 to 1599 |167.9 |10,569 | |Quarterbacks |1600 to 1799 |166.8 |8,173 | |Quarterbacks |1800 and up |158.2 |4,095 | |Quarterbacks |Unrated |141.8 |13,729 | |Running backs |Under 1400 |48.5 |23,898 | |Running backs |1400 to 1599 |43.7 |21,548 | |Running backs |1600 to 1799 |41.5 |16,004 | |Running backs |1800 and up |38.4 |7,896 | |Running backs |Unrated |41.3 |27,771 | |Receivers |Under 1400 |41.6 |34,787 | |Receivers |1400 to 1599 |41.3 |32,478 | |Receivers |1600 to 1799 |41.0 |24,836 | |Receivers |1800 and up |39.2 |12,129 | |Receivers |Unrated |37.9 |39,701 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- band_grad |> mutate( tooltip = paste0( .data$group, ", ", .data$band, ": ", fmt(.data$mean_yds, 1), " yards (SD ", fmt(.data$sd_yds, 1), ") over ", fmt(.data$games), " games" ) ) |> ggplot(aes(.data$band, .data$mean_yds, fill = .data$group)) + geom_col_interactive(aes(tooltip = .data$tooltip), width = 0.8) + geom_pointrange( aes(ymin = .data$lo, ymax = .data$hi), linewidth = 0.7, size = 0.4 ) + scale_fill_manual(values = group_pal, guide = "none") + facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_y") + labs(x = "Opponent band", y = "Mean yards per game") + theme_cfb2nfl() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1)) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### 3.3 Quarterbacks swing the most yards from game to game, but running backs swing the most relative to their own average Each game's residual is its yards minus the baseline, the mean yards of every player with a line in that category in the same season and opponent band. $$\text{residual} = \text{game yards} - \text{baseline (season, band)}$$ Because the baseline already removes season and opponent strength, residuals centre near zero for every group; what differs is their spread, widest in yards for quarterbacks (standard deviation 115 yards) and narrowest for receivers (37 ``` ::: ::: ## 4. Summary The three groups behave differently along all three axes the post looked at. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Question , ~`What the data showed` , "How does production grow across a career?" , paste0("Quarterback median passing yards rose every career season (", fmt(qb_med_1), " to ", fmt(qb_med_max), "); rushing peaked in season ", rb_peak_idx, " and receiving grew slowly after it.") , "How does it change against stronger opponents?" , paste0("Mean yards per game fell most for running backs (", fmt(rb_drop), " yards from the weakest to the strongest rated band); quarterbacks dipped only against the strongest.") , "How much does it swing game to game?" , paste0("Opponent-adjusted residuals spread widest in yards for quarterbacks (SD ", fmt(qb_sd, 1), "), but widest relative to their mean for ", tolower(rel_most), ".") ) |> kable(caption = "Each question and what the data showed.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Each question and what the data showed. |Question |What the data showed | |:----------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |How does production grow across a career? |Quarterback median passing yards rose every career season (119 to 1,706); rushing peaked in season 4 and receiving grew slowly after it. | |How does it change against stronger opponents? |Mean yards per game fell most for running backs (10 yards from the weakest to the strongest rated band); quarterbacks dipped only against the strongest. | |How much does it swing game to game? |Opponent-adjusted residuals spread widest in yards for quarterbacks (SD 115.0), but widest relative to their mean for running backs. | ::: ::: ## 5. Discussion ::: {.callout-important} Production grows across a career for quarterbacks in a way it does not for running backs, whose median peaks in season 4, or receivers, whose median grows slowly after it. Running backs lose the most against stronger opponents, and once opponent strength is removed quarterbacks swing the most yards from game to game, though not the most relative to a typical game. ::: Caveats: the baseline pools every player with a line in the category rather than comparing within position, so a running back's receiving-band baseline mixes in receivers; a position-specific baseline is a natural refinement. Groups are assigned from a player's most frequent roster position and a group is reduced to one signature stat, so a quarterback's rushing or a running back's receiving is set aside. Game-level stats cover 2010 to 2026. Unrated opponents (no Elo, mostly lower-division teams) are kept as their own band rather than dropped. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE) ``` :::
